The '''FX-7 medical assistant droid''' was a [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droid]] manufactured by [[Medtech Industries/Legends|Medtech Industries]] as part of the [[FX-series medical assistant droid/Legends|FX-series]] of surgical assistants and nursing [[Droid/Legends|droids]]. Typically, an FX-7 droid cost 3,500 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. After the FX-7's manufacturing ended, it was only available as used by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back">''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]''</ref>

==Characteristics==
[[File:FX-7droid-RECG.jpg|thumb|left|180px|An FX-7 unit tending to a wounded patient]]

The FX-7 model was a tall, cylindrical unit roughly symmetrical on all sides. It was equipped with a wide array of sophisticated appendages. Twenty retractable manipulator arms were the norm, but because medical needs varied from [[Star system/Legends|system]] to system, Medtech specifically designed the arms to be modular. Its main manipulator arm, which could extend up to one meter, was located near the upper half of the body, featuring a removable grasper able to be replaced with specific tools. The droid's cap-like head, which could rotate 360 degrees, featured a cluster of sophisticated medical [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] and diagnostic equipment. Its main body contained a medicine/anesthesia dispensing hose and a control board manipulator. The standard FX-7 lacked a [[Binary/Legends|droid language]] [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocoder]], but was equipped with an expansion slot allowing for the addition of one. In lieu of vocal communication, the FX-7 had readout screens and a scomp link for direct access to medical computers or other droids. Medtech's conceptual engineers did not consider mobility to be an important factor of the FX-7's design, intending the droid to be placed at a specific medical station. However, an optional [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorcart]], also manufactured by Medtech, allowed the droid to be carried from place to place.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back" />

==History==
The FX-7s proved to be highly effective droids&mdash;so much so that Medtech did not receive a single complaint during the entire production run&mdash;though newer, far superior droids such as the [[2-1B surgical droid/Legends|2-1B surgical droid]] and the [[MD-series medical droid/Legends|MD-series medical specialist droid]] largely made the FX units obsolete by at least [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back" /> Medtech ultimately retired the line, though during the Galactic Civil War, hundreds of FX-7 droids could still be found in the [[Expansion Region/Legends|Expansion Region]] and [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].

FX-7 droids proved particularly useful to the [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credit]]-strapped [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. By the time of Medtech's demise sometime prior to 3 ABY, the Rebellion had secured several warehouses full of surplus FX models and had acquired others through the [[Black market/Legends|black market]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back" />

An [[FX-7/Legends|FX-7]] unit was employed at [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]], where it worked alongside a [[2-1B/Legends|2-1B]] droid. [[Noa Briqualon]] also owned an FX-7 droid, which he kept on his [[Noa Briqualon's starship|starship]]. Many medical assistants were also owned by the [[Xucphra Corporation|Xuchpra]] and [[Zaltin Corporation|Zaltin]] [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] conglomerates on [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]], as they made superior [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]] operators.
